attack_mechanism: The corresponding control/data route is `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op_ex_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`. `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op` generates, transports, or selects `csr_op_i` on this decode path; the implementation qualifies this propagation with `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.id_valid_o`. In the CSR combinational block, `csr_we_int` defaults to one and is cleared only when `csr_op_i == CSR_OP_READ`; WRITE, SET, and CLEAR therefore retain the write enable. Manipulating `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op` so that a decoded READ appears as WRITE, SET, or CLEAR leaves `csr_we_int` asserted for the selected CSR address. A CSR that should only have been read is modified, enabling unauthorized changes to privilege, interrupt, debug, or counter state.

The corresponding control/data route is `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.deassert_we -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.decoder_i.csr_op_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.csr_op_ex_o -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`. `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.deassert_we` participates in that valid/ready or write-deassert decision before the CSR operation reaches `csr_we_int`; the implementation qualifies this propagation with `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.deassert_we`, `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.id_valid_o`. CSR operation and write controls are transferred from ID only on a valid, advancing pipeline cycle; halt and deassert-write logic suppress side effects on killed instructions. Forcing `cv32e40p_top.core_i.id_stage_i.deassert_we` to preserve the write controls of a killed or halted CSR instruction allows its operation code to reach the CSR block. The squashed instruction can assert `csr_we_int` and modify a protected CSR without an architecturally authorized retirement.
